text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A campaign against drug abuse and prostitution in Ho Chi Minh City is to be stepped up.
-- The British Government's Overseas Development Administration has approved a fund of $5 million for a major poverty alleviation five-year programme in the central province of Ha Tinh.

-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet said that new settlers were now prohibited from entering the central highlands and local authorities had responsibility for enforcing the ban to stop further deforestation.
-- Four Laotians and two Vietnamese were arrested for drug trafficking and the authorities confiscated 7.2 kg (15.8 pounds) of heroin, $36,000 and 18 million dong ($1,550).

-- Vietnam's first intensive course on stock markets opened on April 14 in Hanoi. It is being run by the National Stock Exchange Committee in co-ordination with Asia Pacific International Company and Hong Kong University.

-- According to the Government Office, rice exports in March were 200,000-250,000 tonnes, taking the total for the first quarter of this year to 350,000-400,000 tonnes. The government's first-quarter target had been 500,000 tonnes.
